Three choices shape your quote.

The model, the scope and the work. Pick each one, and the quote follows.

1
Which model?
Model

How the job is contracted. EPCC: IAQ delivers everything and answers for the result. EPCM: the owner holds the contracts and IAQ manages them. A single service on its own. Or, for energy, an ESCO contract paid from the savings.

2
Which scope?
Service

What the contract covers. One of the six services, several, or all six. For example procurement only, design only, or design, procure and build.

3
Which work?
Work

Which kind of work the contractor does, which is how the market classifies it: CSA, MEP or process utilities. Most contractors do one. IAQ does all three in house.

Questions clients ask

The questions facility owners ask before they engage IAQ, answered. Any other question, ask.

Choosing a model
How IAQ is engaged, and who answers for what.
4
Which model should I choose?

EPCC when you want one party to deliver everything and answer for the result. EPCM when you hold the construction contracts yourself and want IAQ to manage them. Large multinationals engage EPCM on the biggest programmes.

See EPC
→
What is the difference between EPCC and EPCM?

EPCC is EPC plus Commissioning: IAQ delivers the whole project, commissioning included. EPCM is EPC Management: IAQ manages the project to the same standard, and the owner holds the construction contracts.

Can I buy one service on its own?

Yes. Procurement only, design only, or design, procure and construct. The scope changes; the EPC model still governs how it runs.

Who answers for a system’s performance?

Under EPCC, IAQ: one contract, one party, from the first drawing to a facility proven to operate as intended. Under EPCM the owner holds the contracts and IAQ manages them; the standard the work is held to is the same.

Time and cost
How long each engagement runs, and what is paid when.
4
How long does a facility take?

Typically 12 to 24 months under EPC, depending on the project. Tool hookup is priced and scheduled per tool set.

How is tools hookup priced?

Per tool set. Each set is scoped from the tool maker’s facility requirements, so the price follows the tools you bring in, not the size of the fab.

See PCU & TTI
→
What does an energy contract cost up front?

Nothing. Under Cooling as a Service IAQ funds, builds and runs the chiller plant for a fixed tariff over 10 to 20 years. Under Energy Performance Contracting IAQ funds the upgrade and is paid from the measured savings over 5 to 10 years.

See EFM
→
How are the savings measured?

Against an audited baseline agreed before the work starts. IAQ is paid from the measured saving, so the saving has to be real and has to last.

A live fab
Bringing tools into a fab that keeps running.
4
My fab is live. Can tools be brought in while it keeps running?

That is the PCU & TTI unit. It works in four phases, facilitization, rig-in, hook-up and commissioning, and it carries all six services except maintenance, which it adds when asked.

See PCU & TTI
→
What are the four phases of a tool installation?

Facilitization, before the tool arrives: everything upstream of its connection point is built to the tool maker’s requirements. Rig-in: the tool is uncrated in a de-trash airlock, moved along an agreed route, set, levelled and anchored. Hook-up: each utility is tapped from the facility and connected into the tool, to its own standard. Commissioning: the tool is proven, then released to production.

What do Process Critical Utilities cover?

The systems a production tool runs on: clean dry air, specialty gases and chemical delivery, ultrapure water, process vacuum and exhaust, and waste treatment.

Does PCU & TTI work outside semiconductor?

No. Semiconductor only. Other hi-tech facilities are built and equipped by EPC under the same six services.

After handover
Running and maintaining what was built.
3
What happens after handover?

Maintenance is the fifth service and EFM carries it as its core. What the maintenance team learns goes back into the next design.

See Maintain
→
What does maintenance cover?

Planned care of the plant and systems that keeps the facility at the standard it was handed over at: uptime protected, lifespan protected, records kept.

Does IAQ take on facilities built by others?

Yes. Energy contracts are for facilities already running, and the tools unit is bought on a fab built by IAQ or by others.

Technical: EPCC and EPCM
The two contract models side by side, point by point.
5
Under EPCC and EPCM, who holds the construction contracts?

Under EPCC, IAQ holds them. Under EPCM, the owner holds the individual construction contracts and IAQ manages them on the owner’s behalf.

Who answers for the system performing as intended?

Under EPCC, IAQ answers for it, as the one accountable party. Under EPCM, IAQ manages the project and the owner’s contractors deliver the works.

Is commissioning and start-up included?

Under EPCC it is included in IAQ’s scope. Under EPCM it is coordinated by IAQ.

How long is a typical EPC programme?

Typically 12 to 24 months, under either model, depending on the project.

When is EPCC the better choice, and when is EPCM?

EPCC when you want one accountable party for the whole facility. EPCM when you want direct control of the construction contracts, with IAQ running coordination, programme and cost.
